hero.headline: Neighbors push back on proposed 85-acre Indrio Town Center near I-95 in St. Lucie County
hero.teaser: A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road is moving closer to reality after county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace.
hero.body:
A proposed 85-acre development in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality despite opposition from neighbors concerned about losing the area's rural character. The project, called Indrio Town Center, would bring a mix of commercial and retail space and possibly residential units to land near Interstate 95 off Indrio Road and Russakis Road. The development totals 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space across more than 85 acres, an area equivalent to more than 48 FIFA-standard soccer pitches. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace, with county commissioners expected to vote on the rezoning in August.

Susan Lewis, who has lived near the proposed site for 15 years running a farm rescue on a property that has been in her family for decades, said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. "I have dogs that have 10 acres to run around. I have horses that have 10 acres to run around. It's gone," Lewis said. She added that she and her family moved to the area specifically for its rural character. "We moved here for a reason; this is why we do what we do. We like to be in the wilderness. This is what Florida used to look like," Lewis said.

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. This land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. "It's an overlay district that's trying to allow for tactful development and new communities that embrace the county's rural character, maintain lands for open space and agricultural activities," Benton said. The approach allows for development that considers compatibility and integration with the county's infrastructure needs, quality of life, jobs and connectivity to the interstate and roadway system.

Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will also include open green space and an over 26-acre park. "The design of it incorporates a lot of open space, really keeping that native buffer along Indrio Road," Heinzelmann said. The rezoning still needs approval from county commissioners in August.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County art teacher killed in shooting on Essex Drive, suspect in custody
cards.body:
A 66-year-old Fort Pierce art teacher was shot and killed Tuesday afternoon at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive in St. Lucie County. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office identified the victim as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce, who was taken to a local hospital where he died. The suspect connected to the fatal shooting has been identified as Dale A. Mincey, who remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker.

Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. Tuesday after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. Barnes was transported to a local hospital following the shooting, but he did not survive his injuries. At this time, Mincey is being held on the existing Broward County warrants while the homicide investigation continues.

Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie County schools. The school district released a statement following his death, though the specific contents were not provided in the sheriff's office report. The loss of the longtime educator has impacted the school community, according to the district's response to the incident.

The sheriff's office said the homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. Deputies said based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public. The sheriff's office indicated that additional information will be released as it becomes available. Investigators are continuing to examine the circumstances surrounding the shooting and the relationship between the victim and suspect. The case is being actively worked by homicide detectives in coordination with prosecutors to determine what additional charges may be filed against Mincey in connection with Barnes' death.

cards.headline: Three lawsuits challenge Florida property tax amendment ballot language before November vote
cards.teaser: Save Our Voters, former South Miami Mayor Philip Stoddard, and former lawmakers Jeff Brandes and Al Lawson filed separate lawsuits arguing Amendment Three's ballot language is biased and misleading.
cards.body:
Florida's property tax amendment backed by the state Legislature is now facing a growing legal fight, with three lawsuits challenging whether the ballot language gives voters a fair explanation or a political sales pitch. The lawsuits target Amendment Three, a proposed constitutional amendment placed on the November ballot by state lawmakers. If approved by 60% of voters, the measure would expand non-school homestead property tax exemptions, eventually exempting up to $250,000 of a homestead's value by 2028. It would also limit some future assessment increases on non-homestead property and place new restrictions on how local governments use property tax dollars. Three separate legal challenges have now been filed by nonprofit Save Our Voters, former South Miami Mayor Philip Stoddard, and former lawmakers Jeff Brandes and Al Lawson. Attorney Jamie Cole, who filed the first lawsuit, said the ballot language is very questionable and as biased as bias can be. The lawsuits take aim at several phrases in the ballot summary, including language saying the amendment would save homes from excessive property taxes, protect small businesses, ensure funding for core services and ensure fairness for Florida residents.

State Rep. Toby Overdorf, R-Stuart, said following approval of the measure in early June that relief is coming and the measure puts money back in the pockets of Floridians, provided a 60% vote. House Minority Leader Fentrice Driskell, D-Tampa, said lawmakers wanted to score some political points but are leaving local communities holding the bag. Ron DeSantis said during a recent press conference that he will vote for the amendment but does not plan to lead the campaign because it is not all he was hoping to see. The cases are expected to be consolidated, with a hearing currently set for July 29. If a judge agrees the ballot language is misleading, the Florida Attorney General could be tasked with rewriting the summary.

cards.headline: Indian River County waste management fees jump 93% for condo owners under new contract
cards.teaser: Vero Beach condo owners saw their monthly waste management fees nearly double from $11 to $21 under a new county contract with Waste Management that began in October 2025.
cards.body:
Thomas Clark spoke with WPTV Anchor Mike Trim during a Let's Hear It event in Vero Beach about concerns regarding his monthly condo association bill after his waste management fees jumped nearly double. WPTV brought these concerns directly to the Indian River County Department of Utility Services during a video conference meeting. The county explained the increase stems from a new contract with Waste Management that began in October 2025. The new contract raised average condo association waste management fees from $11 to $21, a roughly 93% increase. Clark told Trim he is not really happy with the increase and believes if the county made a mistake, it should be on their end and they should look at something to help residents out.

County officials say condo owners are getting additional benefits under the new contract. Himanshu Mehta of the Indian River County Solid Waste Disposal District explained that residents can now place bulk items near condo dumpsters, a service that wasn't previously available. Mehta and other county officials emphasized the importance of community involvement in public hearings, noting that this contract was approved during 2024 hearings. Mehta said if Clark or his HOA wanted to invite county officials to a meeting, they are happy to send someone to go over the process in more detail and his team is available to provide that.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County offers free rip current safety training at public pools this summer
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three free sessions using a new rip current simulation machine at local pools to teach proper escape techniques.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County residents and visitors will have the chance to learn life-saving skills this summer through free rip current safety demonstrations at local public pools. The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using their new rip current simulation machine, which creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques. Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager, said education is one of the most effective tools to prevent water-related emergencies. The demonstrations allow participants to experience how a rip current works in a safe, controlled environment while learning skills that could save their life or the life of someone they love.

The county has scheduled three free demonstrations this summer. On July 19, a session runs from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. at Lakewood Park Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants. On July 28, a session runs from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event with no registration required and first-come, first-served. On August 16, a session runs from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants. According to the National Weather Service, there have been 23 rip current fatalities this year so far in the United States. The proper technique when caught in a rip current is to remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until escaping the current, then swim back to shore at an angle.

hero.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team names and logos ahead of August debut season
hero.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League on Wednesday unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The other two teams are the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters.

The WPBL's debut season begins on Aug. 1 in Springfield, Illinois. Games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. Whitmore told The Associated Press at a scrimmage in March that this is just every little girl's dream to play professional baseball, and now for us to actually be with each other there's so much freedom and peace within it. The league hopes to create a space for women's baseball players similar to the one the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League did 70 years ago.

Each team name holds a unique meaning. The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as Firebelle, who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the Queen of the Diamond. The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist.

The Heights logo includes graphic lines surrounding a baseball, mimicking the speed of a fastball and resembling the New York skyline. The Firebells logo fuses a bell with a phoenix. The Queens logo is a capital Q topped with four baseball diamonds. The Hunters logo is an osprey clasping a baseball bat in its talons. The league has been years in the making and is now set to bring women's professional baseball back to the United States for the first time in decades.

cards.headline: US-Belgium World Cup match draws over 30 million viewers, sets US soccer record
cards.teaser: Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match was the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, peaking at 36 million viewers early in the second half.
cards.body:
According to Fox Sports, the match drew more than 30 million viewers. Viewership peaked at 36 million early in the second half of Monday's match. The United States lost 4-1 to Belgium. Telemundo said its Spanish-language broadcast reached 12 million viewers, which NBCUniversal said is a record for a U.S. men's national team broadcast. Interest in Monday's match intensified after FIFA announced that Folarin Balogun would be eligible to play against Belgium despite receiving a red card last week against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The United States' match against Bosnia and Herzegovina also set records. Fox said about 26.4 million viewers tuned in, setting what was then the record for an English-language soccer broadcast in the United States. Telemundo said it drew 9.8 million viewers, the largest Spanish-language audience for a U.S. men's national team match. Fox said its World Cup broadcasts have generated significant interest beyond U.S. matches. The network said last week's Portugal-Croatia match drew more than 11 million viewers, making it the most-watched World Cup match on Fox that did not involve the United States or a final. Fox also said its Mexico-Ecuador broadcast last week drew more than 10 million viewers. Telemundo said its Mexico-England broadcast delivered 23.1 million viewers.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi leads Argentina to 3-2 comeback win over Egypt, advances to World Cup quarterfinals
cards.teaser: Argentina overcame a two-goal deficit in the final 11 minutes to defeat Egypt 3-2, with Messi scoring his eighth goal of the tournament and Enzo Fernandez netting the winner in stoppage time.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi scored his record-extending 21st goal at the World Cup in the 83rd minute to level the score at 2-2 in Argentina's improbable comeback victory over Egypt on Tuesday. Enzo Fernandez scored the winning goal in stoppage time to complete one of the great World Cup comebacks. Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute with only 11 minutes of regulation time remaining after Argentina had trailed 2-0. The defending champions will next face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri. Messi, who was in tears after the final whistle, scored his eighth goal of the tournament. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said he was so emotional and praised the group of players.

Argentina had trailed 2-0 on goals from Yasser Ibrahim and Mostafa Zico. Egypt took a surprising lead in the 15th minute when Ibrahim got ahead of Lisandro Martinez to meet Marwan Attia's cross and head the ball into the bottom corner. Messi missed a chance in the first half when his penalty kick was saved by Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir after Haissem Hassan tripped Nicolas Tagliafico in the box. He later hit the post when the score was 1-0. Despite being the all-time leading scorer at World Cups, Messi has now missed four of eight penalty kicks at the tournament. Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962.

cards.headline: United States eliminated from World Cup after 4-1 loss to Belgium in round of 16
cards.teaser: Belgium's Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal as the Red Devils knocked the United States out of the World Cup on Monday night at Lumen Field.
cards.body:
The United States' hopes for a deep World Cup run at home ended when Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal, helping Belgium expose the Americans' defensive liabilities in a 4-1 win Monday night that earned a quarterfinal berth. While the U.S. was boosted by the presence of star forward Folarin Balogun, whose one-game red-card suspension was controversially lifted by FIFA, American defenders were at fault in a pair of first-half goals and goalkeeper Matt Freese's gaffe gave the Red Devils a third early in the second half. Second-half substitute Romelu Lukaku added Belgium's final goal in the third minute of stoppage time. A crowd of 66,925 at Lumen Field watched as Belgium extended its unbeaten streak to 18 games and will play 2010 champion Spain on Friday at Inglewood, California, for a semifinal berth against France or Morocco.

Malik Tillman tied the score 1-1 midway through the first half with his second free kick goal of the tournament, but the Americans conceded just 61 seconds after the ensuing kickoff. Coach Mauricio Pochettino showed his frustration by kicking a rack in front of the bench, sending four water bottles flying. American star Christian Pulisic could only watch from the bench after injuring his right foot when he hit a boot of Belgium captain Youri Tielemans on a 52nd-minute shot attempt. After winning three games in a World Cup for the first time in this expanded 48-nation tournament, the U.S. failed in its quest to reach the quarterfinals for the first time since 2002 and lost to Belgium for the seventh straight time since a victory at the initial tournament in 1930. All six CONCACAF nations have been eliminated, with the co-hosts U.S., Mexico and Canada all falling in the round of 16.

cards.headline: IOC ends neutral status vetting for Russian athletes ahead of 2028 Los Angeles Olympics
cards.teaser: The International Olympic Committee advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 LA Olympics.
cards.body:
The IOC advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The move was expected since the International Olympic Committee advised two months ago that athletes from Belarus, Russia's military ally in the full military invasion of Ukraine, should be allowed again to compete with their full national identity. The IOC said in a statement after a meeting of its executive board that it stands in solidarity with the Olympic community of Ukraine, which the Olympic movement has supported since the beginning of the war and will continue to do so.

The IOC eased entry requirements to its own events for Russian athletes and teams while provisionally lifting its suspension since October 2023 of the Russian Olympic Committee. The terms of that suspension, imposed when the Russian Olympic body incorporated regional sports councils from occupied regions of Ukraine, no longer applied, the IOC said. Just 32 athletes from Russia and Belarus competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics as approved neutrals and combined to win five medals. The Russian team had more than 300 athletes at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics and won 71 medals. The IOC did not yet approve letting Russian athletes and teams compete with their flag and anthem. That decision will come at an appropriate time, it said. The next Olympic competition is the 2026 Youth Summer Games in Dakar, Senegal opening Oct. 31.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. The event marks nearly two decades of the annual festival celebrating seafood in Indian River County.

The festival is organized by Under The Sun Promotions, Inc., which has produced the event in Vero Beach for 17 consecutive years. The announcement was made on Monday.

The annual festival has become a regular tradition for Vero Beach residents and visitors seeking seafood and entertainment along the Treasure Coast. Under The Sun Promotions has managed the event since its inception.

Specific dates, location details and vendor information for the November 2026 festival will be announced by the event organizers in the coming months.

hero.headline: Neighbors push back on proposed 85-acre Indrio Town Center near I-95 in St. Lucie County
hero.teaser: A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road is moving closer to reality after county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace.
hero.body:
A proposed 85-acre development in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality despite opposition from neighbors concerned about losing the area's rural character. The project, called Indrio Town Center, would bring a mix of commercial and retail space and possibly residential units to land near Interstate 95 off Indrio Road and Russakis Road. The development totals 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space across more than 85 acres, an area equivalent to more than 48 FIFA-standard soccer pitches. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace, with county commissioners expected to vote on the rezoning in August.

Susan Lewis, who has lived near the proposed site for 15 years running a farm rescue on a property that has been in her family for decades, said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. "I have dogs that have 10 acres to run around. I have horses that have 10 acres to run around. It's gone," Lewis said. She added that she and her family moved to the area specifically for its rural character. "We moved here for a reason; this is why we do what we do. We like to be in the wilderness. This is what Florida used to look like," Lewis said.

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. This land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. "It's an overlay district that's trying to allow for tactful development and new communities that embrace the county's rural character, maintain lands for open space and agricultural activities," Benton said. The approach allows for development that considers compatibility and integration with the county's infrastructure needs, quality of life, jobs and connectivity to the interstate and roadway system.

Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will also include open green space and an over 26-acre park. "The design of it incorporates a lot of open space, really keeping that native buffer along Indrio Road," Heinzelmann said. The rezoning still needs approval from county commissioners in August.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County suspect identified in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified Dale A. Mincey as the suspect connected to a shooting that killed a 66-year-old man in St. Lucie County. The fatal shooting happened Tuesday at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. The victim, identified as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce, was taken to a local hospital, where he died. Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie County Schools, and the district released a statement following his death.

Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker. The homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. Based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public, deputies said. Additional information will be released as it becomes available.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County to host free rip current safety training at local pools this summer
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using a new rip current simulation machine to teach proper escape techniques in controlled pool environments.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County residents and visitors can attend free rip current safety demonstrations this summer at local public pools. The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using their new rip current simulation machine, which creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques. On July 19, a session runs from 1 to 4 p.m. at Lakewood Park Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants. On July 28, a session runs from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event with no registration required and first-come, first-served admission. On August 16, a session runs from 1 to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants.

Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager, said education is one of the most effective tools to prevent water-related emergencies. The demonstrations allow participants to experience how a rip current works in a safe, controlled environment while learning skills that could save their life or the life of someone they love. According to the National Weather Service, there have been 23 rip current fatalities this year so far in the United States. Many swimmers make a critical mistake when caught in a rip current by trying to swim directly back to shore, which often leads to dangerous exhaustion. The proper technique is to remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until escaping the current, then swim back to shore at an angle.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Manager Releases Proposed FY 2026-27 Budget
cards.teaser:
Port St. Lucie City Manager Jesus Merejo has released his proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, outlining nearly $975.3 million in spending across all city funds.

The propo
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Manager Jesus Merejo has released his proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, outlining nearly $975.3 million in spending across all city funds.

The proposed budget represents a 12.12% increase from the current fiscal year, which the city says is driven by inflation and capital projects. The general fund budget is proposed at about $230.6 million, an 8.48% increase, or roughly $18 million more than FY 2025-26.

The city's taxable value is also expected to rise. According to the budget brief, Port St. Lucie's estimated certified taxable value increased 5.45%, from $25.5 billion in FY 2025-26 to $26.9 billion in FY 2026-27, due to growth and property appreciation.

Under the proposal, the operating millage rate would remain at 4.6607 per $1,000 of taxable value. The total proposed millage rate would remain 4.9750, including the voter-approved Crosstown Parkway debt service millage of 0.3143.

Residents could see some fee changes. The stormwater fee would increase by $6, bringing the residential rate to $195. The solid waste assessment would increase to $482.16 under the city's contract with its solid waste vendor, though qualified residential homeowners would receive a one-time credit of either $364 or $64. The city also proposes a 3.5% increase in the water rate, while the sewer rate would remain unchanged.

The proposed budget also includes long-term infrastructure planning. The city says capital improvement projects over the next five years are projected to cost about $1.069 billion. The largest portion is for utility system upgrades, listed at $672.7 million. Other planned spending includes $51.1 million for Walton & One, Torino & Tradition Regional Parks and O.L. Peacock Park, $34.8 million for facilities maintenance, $24.5 million for street resurfacing and $9.9 million for sidewalk projects.

The budget brief also notes that Port St. Lucie's long-term debt has declined from more than $1.042 billion in FY 2009-10 to a projected $765 million in FY 2026-27, a reduction of 26.58% over 16 years. The proposed budget includes a net increase of seven positions in the Utility Systems Fund, bringing the city to 1,550.25 full-time equivalent positions.

City Council will review the proposed budget during a workshop July 22-23 at the Community Center, located at 2195 SE Airoso Blvd.

The workshop will also be televised live on the city's website, Xfinity Channel 20 and Blue Stream Fiber Channel 20.
